reasoning_traces.think:
The logarithmic pooling weight (LPW) combines market and structural model forecasts into a single probabilistic estimate, optimizing based on validation performance. It is derived from the principle of minimizing expected log-loss while preserving information from both sources. The Shin de-vigging mechanism corrects for bookmaker margins by estimating the proportion of insider trade, allowing for unbiased comparison between market prices and model predictions. Match leverage measures how much a single game outcome affects the probability of achieving a season-long objective, such as playoff qualification or relegation avoidance. These primitives form a coherent framework for evaluating structural model value relative to market prices, with LPW serving as the benchmark diagnostic, Shin providing margin-free price alignment, and match leverage offering insight into strategic importance of individual games.
